### Checklist

- [x] The bug is reproducible against the latest release or `master`.
- [X] There are no similar issues or pull requests to fix it yet.

### Describe the bug

If an HTTPS request causes a slash redirect, the https schema is not preserved in the "location" header in the response.
This is especially important for environments that don't allow http requests. In such cases all slash-missing requests will fail with a 426 response.

### Steps to reproduce the bug

1. create a server that can handle HTTPS requests
2. create a url "/foo", make sure that redirect_slashes is "True"
3. make an https request to "/foo/"
4. note the response location

### Expected behavior

the "location" header in the response should be to "https://../foo"

### Actual behavior

the "location" header in the response is actually "http://../foo"

### Debugging material

_No response_

### Environment

observed in linux/ python 3.8/ starlette version 0.17.1

### Additional context

_No response_
